newsitem.title: USA: Two N.Y. and N.J. hospitals agree on new alliance.
newsitem.headline: Two N.Y. and N.J. hospitals agree on new alliance.

text.p: Mount Sinai Medical Center of New York City and Saint Barnabas Health Care System of Livingston, N.J., said Wednesday they planned a new alliance.

The pact, which the two hospitals have given themselves a 90-day deadline to finalize, would enable them to work together in medical education, patient care and contracting with managed care providers.

But the two hospitals would remain financially, administratively and medically autonomous, according to the letter of intent, although Saint Barnabas is expected to become a major teaching affiliate of Mount Sinai.

Deregulation of the health care industry and the increased competition between hospitals, which are all chasing managed care patients, have forced a number of small hospitals to close. Others are busily consolidating and finding new partners.

Mount Sinai and New York University in mid-June said that they planned to merge their schools, hospitals, sister institutions, and regional networks, to create a new entity with $2.188 billion in revenues.
